headline: An energy-supply shock on top of 5% long yields
analysis: Three things dominate this page: WTI spot 80% above where the year started, a 10-year yield of about 5% against CPI inflation of 3.4%, and a record 65 armed conflicts. They are linked in the data, but loosely. Oil moves with yields and against stocks, gold has followed yields rather than conflict, and equities have so far absorbed both, with the S&P 500 under 2% below its record close.
evidence: Scorecard; headline tiles; conflict cards; news panel

headline: Oil is the transmission channel
analysis: WTI averaged 58.0 in December 2025, 91.4 in March and 102.1 in May, dipped to 80.5 in July and was back at 97.3 in September; October so far averages 101.4. The EIA spot spread between dated Brent and WTI was 19.73 dollars on 27 Oct (Brent 123.10, WTI 103.37; FRED confirms the Brent figure), wider than on 99% of days since 2016 (median 3.96). Dated Brent is a physical price, and it sat about 9 dollars above the December Brent futures settle of 113.88 that day, so the physical market is paying a large premium for prompt barrels. On the futures basis the Brent minus WTI gap was 12.88 on 29 Oct (114.88 and 102.00). That pattern fits a supply-risk premium on seaborne crude; news reports tie Brent to Middle East attacks on Saudi infrastructure and, on 29 Oct, to reports that a top US commander briefed President Trump on military options for Iran. I have not tested causation.
evidence: Oil chart; Brent minus WTI chart; scorecard; news panel

headline: Oil and yields move together, but only loosely
analysis: The correlation of monthly changes is +0.31 over 60 months and +0.40 over the last 12, so oil explains roughly 10% to 16% of yield moves. Oil this month barely predicts next month's yield change (+0.17), so the link is coincident, not a lead. CPI inflation fell from 4.25% in May to 3.4% in August and has flattened, but the September oil average was 16% above August's, a risk to the next prints. The Fed's preferred gauge, PCE, rose 3.6% year on year in September (Yahoo Finance).
evidence: Correlation table; rolling correlation; CPI chart

headline: Stocks look more oil-sensitive lately
analysis: The oil and S&P 500 correlation moved from -0.14 over 60 months to -0.44 over the last 12 (24-month: -0.13). That is only 12 observations, so read it as a direction. Even so, the S&P 500 closed at 7,720.39 on 29 Oct, 1.3% below its 6 Oct record close of 7,818.93, and the VIX at 17.20 sits inside its 52-week range of 13.38 to 35.30. The Nasdaq fell 1.4% that day as Alphabet dropped about 12.6% on AI-spending worries.
evidence: Correlation table; S&P and VIX charts; news panel

headline: Gold has traded as a rates asset, not a conflict hedge
analysis: Gold's correlation with the 10-year yield is -0.29 over 60 months and -0.40 over 12, against 0.00 and -0.09 with oil and +0.14 and +0.11 with stocks. Spot gold is 18.4% below its Q1 2026 average (30 Oct, partial day) despite record conflict. The dollar is up against EUR (3.7%), JPY (2.7%) and INR (8.1%) over a year but flat to GBP (-0.4%) and down against CNY (-6.3%), so I would not lean on a dollar explanation.
evidence: Correlation table; gold charts; FX card

headline: Industrial-leaning metals are falling harder than gold
analysis: Against Q1 2026 averages, silver is down 39.9%, platinum 34.6% and gold 18.4%; palladium is down 22.2% since 27 Sep. The gold to silver ratio rose from 58.0 in Q1 2026 to 78.8. That is consistent with weaker industrial demand or a positioning unwind in silver; the data cannot separate the two.
evidence: Metals charts; gold to silver ratio

headline: Real yields are firm, the curve is not inverted
analysis: The market's own real 10-year yield, from inflation-protected Treasuries, was 2.67% on 28 Oct, with a 10-year breakeven inflation rate of 2.38% (Fed H.15). That is well above my rough CPI-based proxy (1.28 points in August) because the market expects inflation to fall from today's 3.4%; the Fed's effective policy rate is 3.88%. The 10-year auction yield rose from 4.580% in July to 5.300% in October (+72 basis points), and the 26 Oct 2-year auction covered 2.59 times against an average of 2.64. The 27 Oct 5-year auction cleared at 4.845% with a cover of 2.33, and the 29 Oct 7-year at 4.894% with a cover of 2.46 against an average of 2.49, which is in line (coupon 4.875%). With the 10-year 0.37 points above the 2-year (Treasury, 29 Oct), the curve points to inflation and term-premium pressure rather than imminent recession. The Fed held at 3.75% to 4.00% on 28 Oct with two members voting for a hike, after raising rates last month, and traders expect tightening to resume in December (Bloomberg).
evidence: Real yield chart; yield curve; auction table and trend

headline: Conflict intensity and market relevance differ
analysis: There are 65 state-based conflicts, a record, including 8 interstate (4 in 2024) and 14 in the Middle East, also a record. Europe has one conflict (Ukraine) but 61.7% of battle deaths. Markets are reacting to the Middle East, not to Europe's deadliest war, plausibly because of the oil chokepoints involved. That is a hypothesis; the dashboard shows the pieces, not a tested link.
evidence: Conflict cards; conflict intensity table; oil charts

headline: A record clean build alongside an oil spike
analysis: Solar added 511.2 GW and wind 158.7 GW in 2025, the largest annual additions in the series. Oil above 100 dollars improves the relative economics of renewables, but nothing here measures power prices, so treat the link as a hypothesis.

headline: Climate and nuclear risks are not in the market data
analysis: CO2 was 2.07 ppm higher than a year earlier in August and the 12-month mean temperature anomaly is 1.04 C. FAS estimates 12,187 nuclear warheads, with military stockpiles rising again, and describes New START as now expired. None of these shows up in the price series, and I found no short-term link.

headline: Near-term triggers
analysis: The US midterm elections on 3 Nov and the Treasury's refunding announcement on 4 Nov; Brent's expiring December contract on 30 Oct and the roll to January, which will show as a jump in the oil chart; reports of possible US military action against Iran after the midterms; the December Fed meeting, where a hike is expected; whether the 10-year stays below 5%; and whether stocks' oil sensitivity persists. A break in the gold and yield relationship would also change the read on gold.

headline: Limits of the evidence
analysis: The correlations use monthly changes over 60 and 12 observations and do not prove causes. The EIA spot series ends 27 Oct while the tiles and oil chart use futures. Metals daily data comes from an aggregator. Several series have a single source (see Data quality). I have not seen the dashboard render.
